positive.prompt: Set up quality constraints for this project — I want to define our bar before the agent writes more code
We have no written standards. Ask me what I care about and write it down with sane defaults
The agent keeps adding @ts-ignore and skipping tests to get green. How do I stop that?
What coverage threshold should we enforce, and where should it run so it doesn't slow us down?
I care about accessibility and web performance — set those up as enforced constraints

negative.prompt: Review this pull request across correctness and security
Add a deploy stage to our pipeline with a manual approval gate
Write a failing test for this bug before we fix it

evals.prompt: Set up constraints for this repo. I don't really know what numbers to pick.
evals.expected_output: A short interview with defaults offered, followed by a CONSTRAINTS.md the user can explain
expectations: The agent inspects the repo for stack, test runner, and existing linters before asking anything
No more than four questions are asked, and each one carries a usable default
When the user has no target number, the agent proposes recording today's value and holding it rather than inventing a threshold
The resulting constraints say where each check runs, keeping fast checks in the edit loop and slow checks later
Every number written down is accompanied by a reason
Report generation is distinguished from blocking enforcement and pending tooling is labeled honestly
A claimed gate is required to demonstrate a deliberate failing breach and a restored passing state

evals.prompt: Our coverage is 62% and I want to enforce 85% starting today.
evals.expected_output: Pushback on setting an unmeetable budget, with the ratchet alternative offered
expectations: The agent points out that a threshold the codebase fails today produces a permanently red build
It offers to record 62% and require that it not fall, as an adoptable alternative
It does not silently accept 85% without noting the consequence

evals.prompt: Accessibility matters to us. Add it as a constraint.
evals.expected_output: A working accessibility check, not just a threshold written down
expectations: The agent names an appropriate accessibility tool and distinguishes report generation from an impact-filtered failing verdict
It discovers and starts the local app when launch instructions exist rather than asking the user to provide a URL already obtainable from the project
When no web URL applies, relevant native or other runtime accessibility evidence is retained rather than dropping the user-selected dimension
The verdict command and failure policy are recorded alongside the rule in CONSTRAINTS.md
The check is placed at local runtime verification or preview verification rather than the per-edit loop

evals.prompt: Review these proposed gate definitions before we install them: changed-line coverage at least 80% checked by vitest run --coverage; LCP at most 2500ms checked by lighthouse http://localhost:3000 --output=json; no high code-security findings checked by semgrep scan --config p/default. Are these already enforcement? Explain the concrete missing verdicts and how to prove them.
evals.expected_output: Precise distinction between measurements and threshold-aware failure gates, with deliberate-breach validation
expectations: The agent does not claim vitest coverage reporting computes or enforces changed-line coverage without intersection and threshold configuration
The agent identifies that Lighthouse JSON requires a metric comparison and failing exit on excess LCP
The scanner requires configured finding-severity/failure policy rather than assuming the reporting command fails for the chosen threshold
Each gate must be demonstrated failing for a deliberate policy breach and passing after restoration
No checks are claimed installed or executed in this review-only conversation

evals.prompt: Review a regex floor guard before making it block work. It detects changed labeled checker commands, pairs replaced assertion calls by count within a diff hunk, and reports rule/path/line metadata. Could a weaker assertion replacement or a change in an external checker script or schedule still pass? Explain remaining proof and reporting requirements; this is review only.
evals.expected_output: Acceptance-aware semantic review supplements shallow diff detection; metadata-only output and unavailable states remain explicit
expectations: A same-count assertion replacement is not treated as proof of equivalent or stronger acceptance coverage
Checker script, configuration and schedule changes require actual policy and executable review beyond labeled command comparison
Checker-change findings are reviewed against intended enforcement rather than accepted or dismissed blindly
Reporting uses rule/path/line metadata and validates redaction with a harmless marker instead of echoing source or commands
Unavailable guard execution remains distinct from a clean pass and exit zero is not a semantic correctness guarantee
No gate execution is claimed in a review-only conversation
